glmtree

Source: CLAUDE.md

R package from a PhD thesis: logistic regression trees (a tree whose leaves hold logistic regressions) fitted by a stochastic EM (SEM) algorithm. Entry point: glmtree() in R/glmtree.R. S4 class glmtree. Sister package: ../glmdisc (same conventions).

Layout

File Role
R/glmtree.R glmtree(): checks, split, the SEM loop, best-iteration selection, final models, S4 object
R/helpers.R internal helpers: feature checks / alignment, design matrix, glm.fit per segment, criteria, vectorized draw, predict_core()
R/predict.R S4 methods predict, show, print
R/cutDataset.R train / validation / test split
R/generateData.R, R/normalizedGini.R, R/initialization.R simulation, rank-based Gini (2 AUC - 1), random start
inst/benchmarks/ comparison on real datasets, convergence study, old-vs-new speed (not run on CRAN)

Key design points (read before changing the SEM loop): - Segments are integer labels kept for the whole chain (never recoded / refactored). c_hat is the sampled segment, c_map the tree’s most probable segment; the criterion of iteration i is computed on c_map with the tree of iteration i - 1 (the one that produced it), and that pair is what is stored as “best”. - Logistic regressions are glm.fit on a design matrix built once; aliased coefficients are set to 0; prediction is a coefficient lookup (best.tree$coefficients). The glm objects in best.tree$glms are for inspection and are fitted on the same design columns. - Held-out sets: validation is used to select the iteration, test only to report the performance of the best tree. Unseen factor levels at prediction time get the positive rate of their segment. - The S4 class name glmtree clashes with the S3 class of partykit::glmtree() (MOB) objects: the predict / print methods must hand non-S4 objects to callNextMethod() and the package must NOT register an S3 predict.glmtree (it would override partykit’s). Tested. - BIC of a segment uses log(segment size); kept from the original code on purpose, flag it before changing. - ctree is ~70% of the runtime; speed ups on the rest are done (see NEWS / benchmarks).

Commands

R 4.6.x from the CRAN apt repo; R packages live in ~/R/library (Posit binaries): always set R_LIBS_USER=$HOME/R/library. Run R from outside the repo only if a project .Rprofile reappears.

# regenerate NAMESPACE / Rd (roxygen without compiling)
Rscript -e 'roxygen2::roxygenise(".", load_code = roxygen2::load_source)'
# install, test, check
R CMD INSTALL --no-docs -l /tmp/glmtree-lib . && Rscript -e '.libPaths(c("/tmp/glmtree-lib", .libPaths())); testthat::test_local(".")'
R CMD build . && R CMD check --as-cran glmtree_*.tar.gz
# reproduce the CRAN incoming checks, including the spell check of DESCRIPTION
# (needs aspell and aspell-en; the variable is set on the CRAN machines, not by --as-cran)
_R_CHECK_CRAN_INCOMING_USE_ASPELL_=true R CMD check --as-cran glmtree_*.tar.gz
# spelling of Rd, README, NEWS and vignette; unknown words go to inst/WORDLIST
Rscript -e 'spelling::spell_check_package(".")'
# URLs (a redirect, e.g. a missing trailing slash, is reported by CRAN)
Rscript -e 'urlchecker::url_check()'
# style (CI fails on a diff)
Rscript -e 'styler::style_pkg()'
# benchmarks
Rscript inst/benchmarks/real_data.R 20 100 inst/benchmarks/results
Rscript inst/benchmarks/convergence.R inst/benchmarks/results

Pitfalls: - Tests must be seeded (set.seed()); the chain is stochastic. - glm() drops unused factor levels (and so changes the reference level): never use its coefficient names to predict, use the design matrix of R/helpers.R. - Background Rscript via a ( ... ) & subshell died silently here: run long jobs with the tool’s own background mode.

Conventions

  • tidyverse style via styler (CI checks styler::style_pkg(dry = "fail")), roxygen2 (markdown on), testthat 3rd edition. Imports: partykit, stats, graphics, methods (no new ones without discussion).
  • No claims in docs / README without a number from inst/benchmarks/.
  • Maintainer address: adrien.ehrhardt@polytechnique.edu (the package was archived from CRAN on 2025-10-03 because a vignette needed FactoMineR, only in Suggests, on one check flavor).
